transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-05-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~64 minutes (recording truncated occasionally)
Attendees: Laura Kim (Redwood AE), Olivier Grant (Redwood SE), Sam Ortega (Redwood Solutions); James Carter (Hartwell InfoSec), Maya Singh (Hartwell Compliance), Ethan Rowe (Hartwell Platform), Priya Nair (Hartwell Legal)

Auto-generated summary (may be noisy):
Redwood walked through region-pinning options for EU/US, discussed subprocessors, KMS/HSM key ownership, cross-border failover, SOC2 + ISO artifacts, RBAC and SSO, and next steps to share security pack and run a KMS deep dive. Customer requested contractual language around data residency, subprocessors list, and right to audit.

Topics: data residency, region pin, subprocessors, encryption/KMS, SOC2/ISO, audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC, failover/redundancy

[00:00:00] Laura Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we're gonna do a focused review on region locking and our subprocessor posture. I'm laura from Redwood, with Olly and Sam.
[00:00:08] James Carter: Hi, thanks. James here. Sorry, bit of background — I'm leading info sec for Hartwell, we run custody systems, so residency's a big deal for us.
[00:00:15] Maya Singh: and Maya from compliance, we'll mostly be checking contractual controls and retention.
[00:00:19] Olivier Grant: great, quick agenda: high level architecture, where customer data can reside, region pinning behaviour, standby failover, subprocessors list, KMS options and audit logs. We'll leave time for Qs.
[00:00:28] Ethan Rowe: Sounds good. Also Priya from legal, hi.
[00:00:30] Priya Nair: hi all.

Transcript body (imperfect):
[00:01:05] Olivier Grant: Ok so the runtime — we have a control plane and a separate private data plane for Private customers; for Hosted customers data may be routed regionally. For Hartwell, we recommend Private or Dedicated to ensure region pinning. The key is the model of region pin: you can pin at the org level or route per-project.
[00:01:32] James Carter: When you say pin at org level, do you mean all PII and request bodies will never leave the selected region, even for backups?
[00:01:39] Olivier Grant: Yes — for Private Deployments and Dedicated with VPC peering, you can set a region-affinity policy with soft vs hard pin. Hard pin prevents cross-border replication; soft pin allows failover where necessary and only after explicit escalation. Note: backups can be configured to remain in-region or encrypted and stored cross-region depending on SLAs.
[00:02:01] James Carter: Who manages the KMS keys if we want the EU-only residency? We need to ensure keys are in EU KMS or HSM and that Redwood cannot decrypt.
[00:02:12] Sam Ortega: Good Q. We support customer-managed keys via KMS for our Private offering; you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) from AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or an HSM. We also support Cloud HSM for dedicated appliances. When BYOK is used, Redwood stores only wrapped keys and we never have plaintext key material.
[00:02:30] Maya Singh: is there an option for an on-prem HSM? Some of our regs call for on-prem or dedicated HSM.
[00:02:36] Sam Ortega: Yes, for Private on-prem installs we can integrate with your HSM over secure channels. There is a setup runbook; Olly will share details.
[00:02:42] Olivier Grant: I will add that our audit trail records KMS wrap/unwrap events as metadata; the raw logs do not contain secrets. We keep these logs in the customer region by default for Private customers.
[00:03:05] James Carter: What about subprocessors? We need full visibility — who are you using for storage, backups, monitoring, observability?
[00:03:12] Laura Kim: We've got a maintained subprocessor matrix. Current primary subprocessors listed are BigCloudProvider (compute/storage), CDN partner (edge), monitoring provider and SRE partner. We'll share the full CSV after the call.
[00:03:23] Priya Nair: Do you accept contractual carve-outs for specific subprocessors? For example, if we cannot allow a certain provider to see logs?
[00:03:30] Laura Kim: We can discuss carve-outs; common approach is to contractually prohibit specific subprocessors or require an approved substitute, we'll need legal review.

[00:04:12] James Carter: Cross-border processing — we need assurance that EU customer data will not be processed in the US for inference. How do you handle model selection and routing?
[00:04:23] Olivier Grant: We have routing policies: region-first, cost-first, latency-first. For region-first, requests are routed to region-local pods. If capacity is exhausted, for customer with hard pin we block to keep residency; for soft pin we can failover to a secondary region but only after policy thresholds are hit. You can choose which.
[00:04:46] Maya Singh: That failover policy must be auditable and included in the DPA.
[00:04:50] Laura Kim: agreed — we'll include the failover policy and a sample SLA clause in the follow-up.

[00:05:30] Ethan Rowe: We also want to understand snapshotting and caching — the runtime uses prefix and KV cache, could that cause cross-region copies?
[00:05:39] Olivier Grant: Great detail — KV/prefix caches are local to the serving cluster and we do not replicate caches cross-region for private/dedicated unless explicitly configured for warm standby. Snapshots for model weights are separate and stored in object storage; those can be region-scoped.
[00:06:02] James Carter: Audit logs — retention and format? We need syslog or SIEM-friendly exports, and immutability for a certain period.
[00:06:11] Sam Ortega: We provide audit logs with event types (api.request, auth.login, key.wrap) and can stream to your SIEM via secure subscription. Retention defaults to 90 days for hosted but configurable to customer requirements for Dedicated/Private. We support WORM-like object storage for immutability on request.
[00:06:36] Maya Singh: Are those logs stored in-region?
[00:06:38] Sam Ortega: Yes for Private/Dedicated we store logs in the pinned region by default.

[00:07:05] James Carter: SOC 2 + ISO: do you have reports we can share under NDA?
[00:07:09] Laura Kim: Yes — we will share SOC 2 Type II report and ISO27001 cert under NDA. I'll include the secure link.
[00:07:16] Priya Nair: We will need specific control narratives for encryption at rest, separation of duties, and subprocessor onboarding.
[00:07:22] Laura Kim: we'll provide the control narratives and a sample DPA addendum.

[00:09:00] (noise/overlap)
[00:09:10] James Carter: Question on SSO — SAML, OIDC? Our org uses SAML with SCIM for provisioning.
[00:09:16] Olivier Grant: We support SAML 2.0 and OIDC, and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC: you can map IdP groups to roles in the console; we also support fine-grained token scopes for service-to-service calls.
[00:09:34] Maya Singh: Is there an enforcement point to prevent a user from creating resources in a different region?
[00:09:40] Olivier Grant: Yes, policy engine enforces region assignments and resource creation policies; actions are audited.

[00:12:05] Ethan Rowe: A nit — do you support data residency for embeddings? They can leak PII into vector indices.
[00:12:13] Sam Ortega: We treat embeddings as data just like text — they follow the same residency rules. We can also support encryption at rest for indices and per-customer index isolation.

[00:14:40] Priya Nair: Contractual — can we get a clause for in-region processing and a penalty if cross-border processing occurs without consent?
[00:14:48] Laura Kim: that's often negotiated; we can propose a contract clause and discuss with legal.

[00:18:00] (moderate crosstalk, coffee machine in background)
[00:20:12] James Carter: What about backups for Disaster Recovery — snapshot lifecycle — are they geo-redundant by default?
[00:20:20] Olivier Grant: Default for hosted is geo-redundant; Dedicated/Private can be configured to be in-region only. For in-region-only DR you typically set up a cold standby in the same region or a nearby compliant region.

[00:24:55] Maya Singh: Encryption details — at rest and in transit? TLS, perfect forward secrecy?
[00:25:00] Sam Ortega: TLS 1.2+ with PFS, mTLS for internal service-to-service, at-rest encryption using KMS keys. Customers can opt for BYOK and HSM.

[00:28:30] (transcription glitch) 
[00:28:45] James Carter: Does Redwood ever re-route logs or metrics to a US-based monitoring provider where data could be processed?
[00:28:53] Laura Kim: We can avoid that — for Hartwell we can configure monitoring exports to a customer-owned SIEM in EU.

[00:33:12] Priya Nair: On subprocessors list — we need dates of engagement and data access categories per subprocessor.
[00:33:20] Laura Kim: we'll include those columns in the matrix we share — access category and date engaged.

[00:38:01] Ethan Rowe: How do you handle cross-border law enforcement requests? Do you have a transparency report?
[00:38:08] Olivier Grant: We have a process: requests go through legal and we notify customers when allowed by law unless prohibited. We publish a transparency report and can add contractual obligations for notice where possible.

[00:42:07] Maya Singh: Any limits on data deletion or right to be forgotten?
[00:42:13] Sam Ortega: We support deletion APIs; data deletion propagates across storage within a bounded window. For backups, deletion can be delayed until retention windows expire; we can negotiate shorter retention.

[00:48:30] Laura Kim: Quick recap — items we'll share: SOC2/ISO pack, subprocessor matrix with access categories & dates, region-pin configuration snippet, KMS runbook and HSM options, sample DPA addendum and failover policy.
[00:48:42] James Carter: Good. Also want a short test where you route a few requests regionally and share the logs so we can verify headers and egress locations.
[00:48:51] Olivier Grant: We'll run a test with trace headers and return the log bundle.

[00:52:00] (small delay)
[00:56:20] Priya Nair: Legal ask — please include indemnity carve-outs for subprocessor breaches and a right to audit clause in the DPA.
[00:56:28] Laura Kim: Understood, we'll include proposed language.

[00:58:50] Maya Singh: Any red flags about capacity or latency if we pin region strictly?
[00:58:58] Olivier Grant: If region pin is strict, you trade off bursting to other regions — we recommend reserved Dedicated capacity for peak loads to avoid throttling. We can model expected QPS and suggest Dedicated commit sizes.

[01:01:10] James Carter: Ok that's helpful. timeline — we want to finish security review by end of month.
[01:01:17] Laura Kim: We'll aim to get docs out in 3 business days and KMS deep-dive next week.
[01:01:25] Sam Ortega: I'll own the deep-dive and bring configuration examples.
[01:01:30] Laura Kim: any other questions?
[01:01:34] Ethan Rowe: none from platform.
[01:01:36] Priya Nair: no.
[01:01:38] Maya Singh: no.

[01:01:45] Laura Kim: Great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the pack and book the KMS session for 2025-05-27.
[01:01:51] James Carter: Thanks all.
[01:01:53] (meeting ends)

References / links mentioned: https://redwood.ai/security-pack (shared post-call), redwood-subprocessors.csv (attached), sample-dpa-failover-clause.docx (to be shared)
